comments.body:
Implemented story A (remove inline compact-on-close).

Changes:
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — deleted `_compact_on_close` and its call site; the close tail now ends at scratch cleanup + best-effort push. Left a comment at the removal site recording the measured 13m53s hold, why the 7084 stand-aside probe could not help (the closing process released the lock seconds before its own probe), and where the trigger went.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_on_close_skip_7084.py` — deleted; every test in it exercised the removed function.
- `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` — dropped the two monkeypatches of the removed name (the tests no longer need compaction disabled, which is itself the point).
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_does_not_compact_barbet.py` — new, 4 tests.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — new invariant section I9b 'Compaction runs out of band, never on the close path', plus a correction to I9a (which told operators to avoid closing tickets through a compact-on-close path during a downgrade window — that path no longer exists).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased/Removed entry naming the one user-visible effect: event logs stay unfolded longer, larger on disk, identical in meaning.

RED verified, not assumed: temporarily restoring an inline `compact_cli` call in the close tail fails 2 of the 4 new tests, including the sampler test, which caught the store write lock held while the SNAPSHOT and .retired sources already existed. Restoring the fix makes all 4 pass.

The sampler test's oracle is a forbidden STATE, not a duration: it samples (lock dir exists?, fold artifacts exist?) every 20ms across the close and asserts the two are never simultaneously true. No timing budget, so nothing for the wall-clock-assert gate to reject and nothing to go flaky under load.

Gates so far: 15/15 scripts/check_*.py pass (the three that 'failed' were argument-less invocations of scripts that require flags — re-run correctly, e.g. check_complexity_baseline.py --check reports active=59 new=0 increased=0 stale=0); module-size 0 violations against the 800 cap; make lint and make typecheck clean (518 files); all five generators re-run with no diff. CI's full pytest invocation is running now.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Gate/CI status before push.

Full CI pytest invocation (-m 'not integration and not external' -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300) on the pre-rebase tree: 12600 passed, 60 skipped, 1 FAILED. The failure was MINE and is now fixed: tests/interfaces/store/test_canonical_event_bytes.py asserted cross-producer canonical event bytes and got its SNAPSHOT coverage implicitly, by closing a throwaway ticket and letting compact-on-close fold it (its own comment said 'closing auto-compacts'). With the trigger gone the SNAPSHOT writer stopped running, so the test's own type-coverage guard fired — working exactly as designed.

Fixed by making the fold EXPLICIT (rebar.compact(snap)) rather than incidental, with REBAR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=1 and REBAR_COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS=0 so a small freshly-written ticket actually folds (the default threshold and horizon would both skip it, and a silently skipped fold would drop SNAPSHOT from the coverage set again). Note threshold must be >= 1 — the config coercion rejects 0. The test now states in a comment why the compact is explicit, so the next person does not re-couple it to a close.

That was the only test in the tree coupled to compact-on-close as a side effect.

Rebased onto origin/main, which had moved to ae6f2ac57a 'Pin the gate ticket store to the live store' — change 1700, the verifier store-pinning fix. It composes cleanly: 1700 changes which ticket store the gate READS, this change removes a post-close store WRITE; no shared surface, no conflict. Post-rebase re-verified: complexity baseline active=59 new=0 increased=0 stale=0, mypy clean (518 files), all five generators re-run with zero diff, wall-clock-assert / raw-git-write / comment-hygiene gates clean.

Non-test diff is 115 lines (61 added, 54 deleted), under the 150-line bugfix-size-attestation threshold, and a signed plan attestation is on file regardless.

Local rebar review-code is a no-op in this checkout (verify.enable_code_review is off), so the Gerrit LLM-Review bot is the first code review this change sees. Re-running the full suite on the rebased tree now; pushing once it is green.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Verified -1 on change 1702, triaged and rechecked (not a defect in this change).

Failure: tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py::test_heal_folds_into_the_ref_from_a_detached_head_tracker, ONE shard only (ubuntu-latest py3.11) out of four. git commit-tree aborted with 'error: unable to create temporary file: No such file or directory', so the doctor raised S3DoctorConflict folding a head into the published ref. ubuntu py3.12, ubuntu py3.13 and macos py3.13 all passed the identical code in the same run; all 9 tests in that file pass locally on this exact commit. A logic defect does not pick one interpreter.

Not reachable from this diff: the change touches transition_close.py (deleting compact-on-close), docs/concurrency.md, CHANGELOG.md and three test files. Nothing in it reaches the s3 doctor. Note the integration tier is excluded from CI's main pytest invocation (-m 'not integration'), which is why my local run never exercised this test — worth remembering rather than treating the local run as complete coverage.

The signature is already documented as transient IN THIS REPO. event_append.py:183 defines _TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS including 'unable to create temporary file', and the comment at event_append.py:175 describes exactly this fault — the loose-object temp create under .git/objects/ returning ENOENT on Linux — as 'a transient filesystem hiccup, NOT a data fault — the identical add succeeds on retry (a Gerrit recheck on the same patchset passes)', recorded under bugs vocal-dip-robin / brainy-floral-globefish. The s3 doctor is separately known to attract this fault class: commit aa61323613 routed its _git through the self-healing seam after three CI failures of the same bundle step.

So the recheck is evidence-backed, not a shrug. Posted on 1702 with the full reasoning.

Discovered work, filed as unheedful-custodial-bluebottle (f7da-baae-3c93-47e2), linked discovered_from: the retry that recognises this signature (_with_transient_add_retry) is composed only into event_append._git_add. gitutil.run_git_write — which s3_doctor._git, compaction and the claim/transition writers all use — retries only READ-side signatures ('could not parse head', 'bad object'). A write-side temp-file ENOENT matches nothing there, so it aborts on the first attempt. One fault class, self-healed in one caller and fatal in every other. Deliberately NOT folded into this change: it is a different concern with its own blast radius and deserves its own review.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LANDED and validated live. Change 1702 submitted, merged as 04b78f5e7e (Gerrit rebased it server-side from my local 6faf9c3440). Worktree realigned to the merged commit via the gerrit remote.

LIVE VALIDATION — this ticket's own close, on the merged code:

    23:49:13  COMPLETION_VERDICT cfcb   <- LLM verifier finished (runs outside the lock)
    23:49:24  STATUS cfcb               <- the close write
    23:49:27  SIGNATURE cfcb            <- attestation
    (no COMPACT commit — none exists for this ticket, ever)

The entire post-verify tail took 14 seconds, and there is no compaction lock hold at all. Compare the incident that opened this investigation, same tail on the old code:

    20:35:47  STATUS 271c
    20:35:49  SIGNATURE 271c
    20:35:52  .ticket-write.lock.d created
    20:49:45  COMPACT 271c              <- 13m53s of continuous store-lock hold

One caveat on how to read this, so the number is not overclaimed: the close's WALL CLOCK was 349s, and that is NOT lock hold and never was. It is the LLM completion verifier, which has always run outside the write lock (proven earlier in this investigation, and the reason the original premise of sunlit-cynical-ray was falsified). The metric that moved is the lock-held tail after the verdict: from up to 13m53s down to the three short per-append acquisitions visible above.

Closed with --class=preexisting: the defect long predates this session — compaction has been inline on close since the close gate was built, and bug 7084 measured the same holder at 48.1s before store growth pushed it into minutes.

Closing this unblocked gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk (1fde-becd-942a-4351), story B, which restores an automatic compaction trigger out of band. Moving to it now: with the depends_on prerequisite closed, review-plan will actually run instead of fast-failing.

Also filed from the CI triage: unheedful-custodial-bluebottle (f7da-baae-3c93-47e2), linked discovered_from — the shared git seam does not retry write-side temp-file faults, so one known-transient fault class self-heals in event_append's git add and is fatal for every other store git caller.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Closing a ticket can freeze every other agent's writes to the tickets store for minutes. The
close's post-write tail calls `_compact_on_close` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:92`,
called at `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:526`), which runs compaction;
`compact_txn._compact_locked` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:328`) takes the ONE store
write lock at `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:340` and holds it for the whole fold — read,
reduce, authorship ledger, snapshot write, retire renames, and the git add/commit.

Measured on this host: closing `271c-e88f-3220-4c9b` held `.ticket-write.lock.d` from 20:35:52
until its `ticket: COMPACT` commit (72ff0358f7) at 20:49:45 — 13m53s, one continuous hold.
Three other closes the same hour held 2m27s, 2m27s and 2m41s. Concurrent agents then burn
their acquire budget and lose writes.

Nothing bounds that hold. Inside the store lock every git call goes through `compact_txn._git`
(`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:41`) -> `gitutil.run_git_write`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:472`) -> `_with_index_lock_retry`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:339`), which opens with `_store_git_op_lock`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:365`) — a SECOND per-store advisory flock. Its budgets stack
inside the held store lock: `_STORE_GIT_LOCK_WAIT_S = 30.0`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:209`), `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS = 10`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:125`), each attempt up to `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS = 3`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:418`) children bounded by `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT = 120`
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:468`). `_compact_locked`'s own `timeout=30, attempts=2` bounds
only ACQUIRING the store lock, never HOLDING it. The 7084 stand-aside probe
(`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:121`) cannot help the closing process, which
released the lock ~3 seconds earlier so the store always reads free.

## Approach
Take compaction off the close path entirely: delete `_compact_on_close` and its call site so a
close ends after signing, the force-close audit comment and scratch cleanup. This alone
restores close lock-holds to the seconds the other three acquisitions already take (sidecar
append, `txn.transition_core`, SIGNATURE append), because compaction is the only unbounded
holder in the tail.

This is safe because compaction is OPTIONAL housekeeping, not a correctness step — the
function's own docstring already states it (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:92`: a
skip is a NO-OP for correctness, the raw events stay live and the next compaction folds them),
and `_compact_on_close` already skips itself whenever the lock is busy. An unfolded event log
is completely valid; the reducer replays it. So removing the trigger changes performance and
store size, never stored state.

Compaction itself is NOT removed: `rebar compact <id>` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:65`)
stays exactly as it is, and the scheduled out-of-band sweep that becomes the standing trigger
is the follow-up ticket that `depends_on` this one. Landing this first is deliberate: it is
the whole P0 fix, it is small enough to review as one change, and it unblocks every stalled
agent today rather than after the sweep is built. The interim cost is that ticket event logs
grow until the sweep lands — accepted, bounded by that follow-up, and recoverable at any time
with a manual `rebar compact`.

Deleting the function also removes the only production caller of
`rebar._store.lock.write_lock_is_busy` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:214`). That function STAYS:
it is a documented store-API probe with its own test suite
(`tests/unit/test_write_lock_busy_probe_7084.py`), so this is not dead code to remove here.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — delete `_compact_on_close` and its call site;
  drop the now-unused local imports it owned.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_on_close_skip_7084.py` — delete: every test in it
  exercises the removed function.
- `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` — drop the two `monkeypatch.setattr(transition_close,
  "_compact_on_close", ...)` lines (`:285`, `:313`) that patch the removed name.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_does_not_compact_barbet.py` — new regression test.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — update the compact-on-close description to say compaction is
  out-of-band.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — record the behaviour change.

## Testing
- A close of a ticket whose event count is far above the compaction threshold writes NO
  SNAPSHOT, retires NO source, and produces no `ticket: COMPACT` commit — the events stay live
  and the ticket still reduces to the same state as before the close.
- A background sampler polling `.ticket-write.lock.d` every 20ms across a full close observes
  the lock only in short bursts, and never across a span that includes a compaction fold; the
  close's own `ticket: STATUS` commit still lands.
- `rebar compact <id>` on that same ticket still folds it normally afterwards, proving
  compaction is intact and only its trigger was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Closing a ticket performs no compaction — a test asserts that after
      `transition <id> in_progress closed` the ticket dir contains no `-SNAPSHOT.json`, no
      `*.retired` source, and the tracker log has no `ticket: COMPACT <id>` commit.
- [x] The close still produces its normal artifacts — the same test asserts the `ticket: STATUS`
      commit landed and the reduced ticket status is `closed`.
- [x] Compaction still works when invoked directly — a test runs `rebar compact <id>` on the
      just-closed ticket and asserts the SNAPSHOT is written and the sources are retired.
- [x] `_compact_on_close` no longer exists — a grep of `src/rebar` for the symbol returns no
      match, and no test patches it.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` no longer describes compaction as running on close, and the full
      local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.

delete: every test exercises the removed function
drop the two monkeypatches of the removed _compact_on_close name
new regression test: a close writes no SNAPSHOT and holds the lock only in short bursts
compaction is no longer triggered on close
